name: Hydra commit by API
description: Create a commit without a git push: blob -> tree -> commit -> ref, entirely over the brokered forge REST API. Carries the two safety rails git push used to provide for free — see openspec/changes/hydra-flows-first-port tasks 2.1 and 2.5.

$comment: 🔑 THE TWO RAILS ARE THE POINT, not the blob/tree/commit chain.
`git push` refuses a non-fast-forward for free. commit-by-API does not, and
`base_tree` OVERWRITES rather than merges — so a tree built against a base
that has since moved silently reverts every file the caller did not send, and
the resulting commit looks perfectly clean. That happened for real during the
nc-vue migration: two files lost an import and a template gate, caught only by
running the full suite.
tip-gate   re-reads the branch tip immediately before the tree is built and
refuses if it no longer equals the base the commit is parented on.
diff-gate  compares the produced commit against the base and refuses to move
the ref unless exactly the expected number of files changed.
Both were exercised live on 2026-07-31 against a throwaway branch:
the diff-gate REFUSED a run whose commit changed nothing (the ref did not
move), and PASSED the next one (blob 201, tree 201, commit 201, ref moved
0acaec6b -> ac1c467f). Two commits existed on GitHub with no git push anywhere.
⚠️ `expectedFiles` is the caller's assertion about its own change. It is not a
formality: it is the only thing that distinguishes 'my one file landed' from
'my tree quietly reverted four others'.
⚠️ Getting here needed two OpenRegister fixes, both found by running it:
openregister#2231 — the broker read `..` anywhere as traversal, so GitHub's
`compare/{base}...{head}` was denied and the diff rail could not be built.
openregister#2232 — a stop on the branch a router did NOT choose still fired,
so the happy path reported `failed` with the rail's own refusal message.

config.$comment: The rail must PROVE the tip is where the commit is parented, and an unanswered forge proves nothing. `==` made this fail OPEN in exactly the situation it exists for: with both reads empty, `null == null` is true and the gate reported `safe`, so 'the recheck never happened' was indistinguishable from 'the branch has not moved'. Hence two conditions, not one. `!!` requires the re-read tip to actually be a sha — an absent read and an empty string both refuse — and `===` then requires the base to be that same sha with no type coercion. Requiring only the tip is sufficient: if the tip is a non-empty string, `===` can only hold when the base is the identical non-empty string.

Same failure as the tip-gate, one node later and with the ref move behind it. `length` of an absent `cmp.body.files` is 0, an absent `expectedFiles` is null, and `0 == null` is TRUE — so a caller that forgot the assertion, or a compare that returned nothing, routed to `clean` and moved the ref. The assertion is now required to BE one: `> 0` rejects both the absent caller and the degenerate 'I expect zero files to change' (which is never a reason to move a ref), and `===` then compares counts without coercion. Measured through the real SetFieldsNode on the deployed `hydra-record-stage/package-commit`: `expectedFiles` arrives as integer 1, so `===` against `length` holds on the working path.

config.message: The branch tip moved while the commit was being built. Refusing to base a tree on a stale parent.
The produced commit touches more files than were sent. base_tree overwrites rather than merges, so this would silently revert somebody's work. Refusing to move the ref.
